findings.issue: The two clause-(1) resolvers are NOT logically byte-equivalent for one input class. Single resolves ONE matched identity by priority (auditMatchSlug = actorSlug-if-in-track ELSE distinct-fallbackSlug-if-in-track) and gates THAT identity's active status. Batch gates BOTH independently and ORs them: (actors.has(actorSlug) && actorSlugActive) || (fallbackSlug distinct && actors.has(fallbackSlug) && fallbackSlugActive). They diverge exactly when actorSlug is in the audit track AND deactivated AND a distinct fallbackSlug is ALSO in the track AND active: DETAIL (single) DENIES via clause 1 (picks actorSlug by priority, which is dead), LIST (batch) GRANTS via the fallback branch. LIST being more permissive than DETAIL is the wrong direction for a security gate. HOWEVER this is UNREACHABLE in production: both call sites pass fallbackSlug=undefined (processes.ts:963 isInstanceParticipant with 5 positional args; processes.ts filterProjectionsByReadVisibility with 7 args -> isInstanceParticipantBatch fallbackSlug=undefined). Under fallbackSlug=undefined the two are PROVABLY byte-equivalent: grant = actorInTrack && actorActive on both paths (verified by case analysis over A/F/aActive/fActive). So this is a latent contract divergence in a currently-dead parameter, not a live authority-path split.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking (unreachable via current callers). Before ever wiring a real fallbackSlug to either caller, align the batch tie-break to the single's matched-identity-priority (evaluate actorSlug-in-track first and only fall to fallbackSlug when actorSlug is NOT in the track), or document the deliberate 'any matched active identity' batch semantics. Equivalence for fallbackSlug=undefined (the shipped behavior) holds today.
